entities.summary: Liu Hong (129-210 CE), courtesy name Yuanzhuo, was a Chinese astronomer, mathematician, and politician who lived in the late Eastern Han dynasty. He was born in Luoyang, Henan Province, during the reign of Emperor Zhi of Han. Liu Hong developed a work on predicting the passage of the moon, which was in use during the Three Kingdoms period of China. His contributions to astronomy and mathematics were significant, as they helped to improve the accuracy of lunar eclipses and the calculation of solar years. Liu Hong's legacy can be seen in the work of later astronomers and mathematicians, who built upon his discoveries and refined his methods. Despite his significance, Liu Hong's life and work are relatively unknown outside of China, highlighting the importance of further research and discovery. Liu Hong's story is a testament to the power of human curiosity and the impact that individual contributions can have on the development of a field.
